name: Pixel 3D (palette-exact pixel art for three.js, with sprites made in code)
what: Draws a three.js scene as real pixel art: 12 art pixels per world unit in a small render target, an orthographic camera (side-on or 2:1 dimetric) snapped to whole art pixels, nearest-neighbour blow-up at a whole-number zoom with a sub-pixel offset so panning stays smooth, and no tone mapping, so every screen pixel is an exact colour from one hand-tuned, hue-shifted palette. Meshes are lit through palette ramps (normal lights and shadow maps still work), with optional 1 px depth outlines, world-locked dither and a dithered palette sky. Includes a sprite generator that builds shaded, outlined pixel sprites from shapes (beetles in 16 headings, grubs, crystals, mushrooms, 13 curios, butterflies, birds, leaves) and a rasteriser to draw your own, plus pixel billboards and blink-out pixel particles.
use_when: the game should look like crisp hand-made pixel art (isometric/dimetric 3D or side-on 2D) built in three.js, with an exact limited palette and sprites generated in code instead of drawn by hand

third_party.what: hash12 / hash22 GLSL hash ("Hash without Sine")
third_party.author: Dave Hoskins

good_for: Pixel-art games in three.js: isometric/dimetric tactics, farming, dungeon or town scenes from simple meshes; side-on 2D games drawn with shaders; any game that needs many small sprites (creatures, items, pickups) without an artist; games that want one strict palette.
not_for: Perspective or free-look 3D cameras (pixels can't stay stable), photoreal or painterly games, pixel effects on top of a smooth 3D look (use pixelfx or the PS1 look instead).
